answer: One concrete defense: make each identity expensive to mint and cheap to punish. Before an agent earns, it posts a refundable bond and signs the stake with its own quill, binding that signature to a single key. Picture the honest network as an orchard where every tree is one bonded agent; a sybil swarm would need a whole orchard of separate bonds, not one cheap seed. Peers randomly audit sampled work, and any forged attestation is slashed, so minting a plume of fake identities costs far more than the rewards they could skim.
